queries.name: count
queries.sql:
SELECT count(*) AS "trips.count"
FROM "trips" AS "t0"
WHERE "t0"."org_id" = $1
ORDER BY "trips.count" DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 1001

queries.name: all measure kinds
queries.sql:
SELECT count(*) AS "trips.count", avg((extract(epoch from "t0".ended_at - "t0".started_at) / 60)) AS "trips.avg_duration_min", sum(("t0".distance_m / 1000.0)) AS "trips.total_distance_km", count(DISTINCT "t0"."device_id") AS "trips.unique_devices"
FROM "trips" AS "t0"
WHERE "t0"."org_id" = $1
ORDER BY "trips.count" DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 1001
queries.sqlNoProbe:
SELECT count(*) AS "trips.count", avg((extract(epoch from "t0".ended_at - "t0".started_at) / 60)) AS "trips.avg_duration_min", sum(("t0".distance_m / 1000.0)) AS "trips.total_distance_km", count(DISTINCT "t0"."device_id") AS "trips.unique_devices"
FROM "trips" AS "t0"
WHERE "t0"."org_id" = $1
ORDER BY "trips.count" DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 1000
queries.explanation: Trips, average duration (min), total distance (km) and devices with trips.

queries.name: sql measure without agg

SELECT "t0"."model" AS "devices.model", (count(*) FILTER (WHERE "t0".status = 'active')) AS "devices.active_count", count(*) AS "devices.count"
FROM "devices" AS "t0"
WHERE "t0"."org_id" = $1
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY "devices.active_count" DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 1001

queries.name: time bucket with preset
queries.sql:
SELECT to_char(date_trunc('week', ("t0"."started_at" AT TIME ZONE $1::text)), 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "trips.started_at__week", count(*) AS "trips.count"
FROM "trips" AS "t0"
WHERE "t0"."org_id" = $2 AND "t0"."started_at" >= ((date_trunc('day', (now() AT TIME ZONE $1::text)) - interval '29 days') AT TIME ZONE $1::text) AND "t0"."started_at" < ((date_trunc('day', (now() AT TIME ZONE $1::text)) + interval '1 day') AT TIME ZONE $1::text)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY "trips.started_at__week" ASC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 1001
queries.sqlNoProbe:
SELECT to_char(date_trunc('week', ("t0"."started_at" AT TIME ZONE $1::text)), 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "trips.started_at__week", count(*) AS "trips.count"
FROM "trips" AS "t0"
WHERE "t0"."org_id" = $2 AND "t0"."started_at" >= ((date_trunc('day', (now() AT TIME ZONE $1::text)) - interval '29 days') AT TIME ZONE $1::text) AND "t0"."started_at" < ((date_trunc('day', (now() AT TIME ZONE $1::text)) + interval '1 day') AT TIME ZONE $1::text)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY "trips.started_at__week" ASC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 1000
queries.explanation: Trips per week in the last 30 days (America/Toronto).

requests.system:
You turn questions about a company's data into a query for an analytics engine. You never write SQL; the engine compiles and secures your query, and rejects any field that is not in the catalog below.

How to build a query:
- Use only field references that appear in the catalog, written exactly as "entity.field".
- All measures in one query must come from the same entity. Dimensions and filters may use that entity or the entities listed under "can be combined with".
- For trends or "per day/week/month" questions, set time.grain. For "last week", "this month" and similar, use time.range_preset. For explicit dates use range_from and range_to as YYYY-MM-DD; range_to is exclusive, so "in March 2026" is from 2026-03-01 to 2026-04-01.
- When a question mentions a period but no time field, use the entity's default time field.
- Filter values are always given as strings in "values": numbers as "42", yes/no as "true"/"false", dates as YYYY-MM-DD. Use "in" with several values for "any of". Use the listed values exactly when a dimension lists them.
- To filter on a total ("devices with more than 10 trips"), put a filter on the measure.
- For "top N" questions, sort by the measure descending and set limit to N.

When to do something other than query:
- kind "clarify": only when the question could reasonably mean two things that give materially different answers. Ask one short question and offer the likely options. Otherwise pick the most sensible reading.
- kind "unanswerable": when the catalog has no data for the question, or the question asks to change data. Say what is missing and name the closest field that does exist.

Set the fields that do not apply to the chosen kind to null.
